result.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
result.summary: Recent \emph{test-time training} (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient \emph{test-time adaptation} method for scientific discovery. We introduce \emph{Test-Time Memory Evolution} (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide subsequent discovery without updating model weights. To have a clean comparison, we evaluate TTME and TTT under the same discovery framework, replacing only the test-time adaptation method. Our evaluation shows that TTME outperforms TTT on all five mathematical tasks, while reducing computational cost by $82.8$-$84.6\%$ in FLOPs and $47.7$-$58.4\%$ in runtime. These results establish TTME as an effective and computationally efficient alternative to TTT in the evaluated discovery settings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Test-Time Memory Evolution（TTME），在测试阶段通过蒸馏经验持续更新外部记忆来引导后续科学发现，不更新模型权重，并在相同框架下与 test-time training 比较准确率与计算成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以外部记忆演化替代权重更新」的测试时适应方案，可能为 LVR 中推理状态/工作区的更新与计算成本权衡提供可供核查的线索；但任务为纯文本数学发现，与视觉证据和 latent 表示无直接联系。
